decisions.rationale: Leading Swampert and Pelipper establishes immediate weather control and Swift Swim pressure. Archaludon in the back abuses Rain with single-turn Electro Shots, while Garganacl provides defensive insurance via Wide Guard against Charizard Y's Heat Wave.
decisions.notebook: Plan: Lead Swampert and Pelipper with Archaludon and Garganacl in reserve. Swampert provides physical damage and Mega Swift Swim pressure. Pelipper sets Drizzle and Tailwind. Archaludon abuses Rain with instant Electro Shot. Garganacl provides Wide Guard against opposing spread moves like Charizard Y's Heat Wave.

decisions.rationale: Charizard-Y plus Venusaur immediately overturns rain, denies Swift Swim, and creates Solar Beam/Chlorophyll pressure into the Water-Ground core. Raichu is the best reserve into Pelipper/Archaludon and offers speed control; Tauros supplies Intimidate and physical cleanup versus Swampert and Tsareena.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 preview selection: lead Charizard + Venusaur; bring Raichu + Paldean Aqua Tauros. Core objective is Mega Charizard Y weather control to overwrite Drizzle and shut off Mega Swampert Swift Swim, enabling Chlorophyll Venusaur. Preserve Raichu for Pelipper/Archaludon and Electroweb/Encore lines; preserve Tauros for Intimidate cycling and physical rain-core pressure. Be cautious using priority if Tsareena is active due to Queenly Majesty.

decisions.rationale: Charizard Y will Mega Evolve and set Sun with Drought, enabling Chlorophyll for Venusaur and 1-turn Solar Beam/Energy Ball targeted at Swampert. Swampert uses Protect + Mega Evolve to completely block all incoming attacks and safely obtain its Mega stat boosts. Pelipper switches to Archaludon, which resists Grass 4x and is immune to Poison. Preserving Pelipper allows us to switch it back in on a later turn to re-trigger Drizzle, overwriting Sun with Rain for Swift Swim.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent led Charizard + Venusaur into Swampert + Pelipper. Charizard has Charizardite Y (Drought). Preserving Pelipper in reserve allows re-setting Drizzle to remove Sun and enable Swift Swim Swampert.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve to replace rain with sun before attacks, removing Swift Swim and activating Chlorophyll. Sleep Powder pressures Pelipper’s Tailwind/Hurricane while Solar Beam heavily threatens Mega Swampert; Venusaur’s Focus Sash covers an Ice Punch response if Swampert survives the roll.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: Mega Charizard Y is primary weather control against Pelipper + Mega Swampert; sun removes rain’s Water boost and Swift Swim while enabling Chlorophyll Venusaur. Preserve Raichu for Pelipper/Archaludon pressure, speed control, and Encore; preserve Aqua Tauros for Intimidate cycling and physical matchups. Avoid priority lines while Tsareena is active because of Queenly Majesty. Mega Charizard Y Solar Beam into Mega Swampert is a possible but not guaranteed OHKO across legal opposing bulk; pair pressure or plan for a surviving Swampert when necessary.

decisions.rationale: Switching Swampert to Pelipper sets Rain before any moves execute, overriding Sun and removing Chlorophyll speed. In Rain, Solar Beam requires a charge turn and Fire attacks are weakened. Rain also enables Archaludon's Electro Shot to fire in a single turn with a +1 SpA boost, guaranteeing an OHKO on Charizard-Mega-Y (101.6-179.1%). Swampert stays preserved to sweep under Rain later.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent led Charizard-Mega-Y + Venusaur into Swampert + Pelipper. Preserving Pelipper in reserve allows re-setting Drizzle to remove Sun and enable Swift Swim Swampert. Archaludon's Electro Shot charges instantly in Rain and KOes Charizard-Mega-Y.

decisions.rationale: Solar Beam guarantees the Mega Swampert KO if its reduced-rate Protect fails, while Venusaur’s guaranteed Speed lets Sleep Powder deny Archaludon’s dangerous Electro Shot 75% of the time. Doubling Swampert is unnecessary because Solar Beam alone already covers its full legal bulk range.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Under Mega Charizard Y sun, Charizard Solar Beam is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Swampert across legal bulk, and Venusaur Energy Ball is also a guaranteed OHKO. Venusaur’s Chlorophyll Speed guarantees it moves before Archaludon. Archaludon Electro Shot versus full-health Mega Charizard Y is 82.6–118.7%, so sleep/pressure on it is valuable. Preserve Raichu for Pelipper/Archaludon pressure, speed control, and Encore; preserve Aqua Tauros for Intimidate cycling and physical matchups. Avoid priority lines while Tsareena is active due to Queenly Majesty.

decisions.rationale: Charizard-Mega-Y is the opponent's sole weather setter (already Mega Evolved turn 1) and is 2x weak to Water and Electric. In Rain, Archaludon's Electro Shot charges instantly for a guaranteed OHKO if it wakes up, retargeting Venusaur if Pelipper acts second. Pelipper's Hydro Pump in Rain deals 98.4-172.5% to Charizard, giving a strong chance to eliminate Charizard this turn even if Archaludon stays asleep. Pelipper holds Focus Sash and comfortably survives any attack.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent led Charizard-Mega-Y + Venusaur into Swampert + Pelipper. Charizard Mega Evolved Turn 1 (Drought exhausted). Rain is active (4 turns left). Mega Swampert in back has Swift Swim (208 Speed) and OHKOes Charizard with Rain Waterfall.

decisions.rationale: Charizard is committed to Solar Beam. Sleep Powder on Pelipper denies its rain-accurate Hurricane/Hydro Pump line and preserves momentum; Archaludon is already asleep, while attacking Pelipper is not a reliable KO through its bulk and Focus Sash.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: In Mega Charizard Y sun, Charizard Solar Beam and Venusaur Energy Ball each guaranteed OHKO Mega Swampert across legal bulk. Archaludon Electro Shot versus full-health Mega Charizard Y is 82.6–118.7%, so sleep or other pressure is valuable. Preserve Raichu for Pelipper/Archaludon pressure, speed control, and Encore; preserve Aqua Tauros for Intimidate cycling and physical matchups. Avoid priority lines while Tsareena is active due to Queenly Majesty. Rain halves Solar Beam damage; versus Pelipper, Mega Charizard Y Solar Beam is 23.4–46.7% and Venusaur Energy Ball is 41.9–83.0%, so their combined damage is not a guaranteed KO.

decisions.rationale: Raichu is the strongest replacement into Pelipper plus sleeping Archaludon: it threatens Pelipper immediately, can absorb Archaludon’s Electric attacks with Lightning Rod, and preserves Tauros for later physical pressure and Intimidate.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: preserve Raichu where possible for Lightning Rod protection versus Archaludon/Pelipper, Fake Out, Electroweb, and Encore. Preserve Aqua Tauros for Intimidate cycling and physical endgames; its Wacan Berry can matter versus Electric pressure. Tsareena’s Queenly Majesty blocks priority against its side, so do not rely on Fake Out or Aqua Jet while it is active. Rain weakens Charizard’s Fire damage and removes Solar Beam’s one-turn charging benefit; Pelipper is the key weather setter. Venusaur’s Grass attacks pressure Mega Swampert strongly, while Sludge Bomb is ineffective into Archaludon.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper is vulnerable at 58% HP to Raichu's fast Electroweb or Fake Out + Venusaur hit. Protect is 100% reliable here to keep Pelipper alive, preserve Rain, and set up Tailwind or Hurricane on Turn 5. Switching into Swampert or Garganacl is dangerous due to Venusaur's Energy Ball. Archaludon takes minimal damage from Raichu and Venusaur, so if it wakes up from sleep this turn, Draco Meteor into Raichu chunk/OHKOes Raichu (70.7-137.8%) and pressure opponent's main disrupter.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent led Charizard-Mega-Y + Venusaur into Swampert + Pelipper. Charizard Mega Evolved Turn 1; Rain re-established Turn 2. Charizard fainted Turn 3 to Pelipper Hydro Pump. Opponent brought in Raichu (Sitrus Berry, LightningRod, Fake Out/Electroweb/Encore). Venusaur has Focus Sash and Chlorophyll, carrying Energy Ball/Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder. Mega Swampert in back ready to sweep once Venusaur is neutralized or in Rain.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out guarantees Pelipper cannot act this turn, while Energy Ball gives the best immediate chance to remove it. Raichu also preserves Lightning Rod coverage against a potential waking Archaludon Electro Shot; Venusaur survives a noncritical Flash Cannon from full.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Mega Swampert (Adamant, Swampertite), Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash, Drizzle; Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect), Archaludon (Modest, Wise Glasses, Stamina; Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect), plus unrevealed Tsareena, Galarian Slowking, Garganacl. Tsareena Queenly Majesty blocks priority while active. Preserve Raichu for Lightning Rod, speed control, Fake Out, and Encore; preserve Aqua Tauros for Intimidate cycling and physical endgame. Venusaur Grass attacks are key Mega Swampert pressure; Sludge Bomb does nothing to Archaludon.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Archaludon uses Protect to block incoming Close Combat from Tauros and Energy Ball/Sleep Powder from Venusaur. Pelipper targets Tauros with a 100% accurate Rain-boosted Hurricane. Tauros holds Wacan Berry (not Focus Sash), so 90.1-176% Hurricane has a high chance to OHKO it. Removing Tauros neutralizes opponent's physical offense, leaving Venusaur which cannot threaten Archaludon.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent led Charizard-Mega-Y + Venusaur into Swampert + Pelipper. Charizard fainted Turn 3; Raichu fainted Turn 4. Opponent has Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Wacan Berry, Intimidate, CC/Liquidation/Aqua Jet/Protect) and Venusaur (Focus Sash, Chlorophyll, Energy Ball/Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder/Protect). Mega Swampert in back outspeeds both in Rain (208 Speed vs max 167 Tauros / 132 Venusaur).

decisions.rationale: Tauros is guaranteed faster than both foes and Close Combat gives the only meaningful immediate chance to remove Archaludon (60.9–106.7%). Sleep Powder on Pelipper has a 75% chance to deny Hurricane/Tailwind this turn; Energy Ball is only a possible, not guaranteed, KO from its shown damage range.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent brought Mega Swampert (Adamant, Swampertite), Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash, Drizzle; Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect), Archaludon (Modest, Wise Glasses, Stamina; Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect), plus unrevealed Tsareena, Galarian Slowking, Garganacl. Tsareena Queenly Majesty blocks priority while active. Preserve Raichu for Lightning Rod, speed control, Fake Out, and Encore; preserve Aqua Tauros for Intimidate cycling and physical endgame. Venusaur Grass attacks are key Mega Swampert pressure; Sludge Bomb does nothing to Archaludon. Tauros (167) is faster than revealed Pelipper and Archaludon outside priority; Venusaur is faster than Pelipper but its order versus Archaludon is EV-dependent. Aqua Tauros Close Combat into Archaludon is a possible but not guaranteed OHKO.

decisions.rationale: Switch sleeping Pelipper to Garganacl to preserve Drizzle for later turns. Archaludon uses Electro Shot on Tauros-Paldea-Aqua: in Rain Dance, Electro Shot fires in 1 turn, boosting Archaludon's Special Attack to -1 before attacking, consuming Tauros's Wacan Berry and dealing heavy super-effective damage. Archaludon comfortably survives Tauros's Close Combat (max 95.1%), triggering Stamina for +1 Defense.
decisions.notebook:
Game 1: Opponent brought Charizard-Mega-Y (Timid, fainted), Venusaur (Modest, Focus Sash, Energy Ball/Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder/Protect), Raichu (Timid, fainted), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Jolly, Wacan Berry, Intimidate, CC/Liquidation/Aqua Jet/Protect). Unbrought: Kingambit, Sableye.
Mega Swampert in Rain (208 Speed) outspeeds Tauros (132-167) and Venusaur (100-132). Preserving Pelipper allows resetting Rain with Drizzle.

decisions.rationale: Tauros is guaranteed to move before Archaludon; Close Combat has a meaningful OHKO chance and otherwise leaves it in range. Sleep Powder targets the more durable long-term threat, preventing it from exploiting Stamina and buying the second Close Combat if it survives. Pelipper is already asleep and Venusaur naturally outspeeds it.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent roster/set information: Mega Swampert (Adamant, Swampertite); Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash, Drizzle: Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect); Archaludon (Modest, Wise Glasses, Stamina: Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect); Tsareena (Adamant, Miracle Seed, Queenly Majesty: Power Whip/High Jump Kick/Knock Off/Helping Hand); Galarian Slowking (Calm, Sitrus Berry, Regenerator: Sludge Bomb/Chilly Reception/Psychic Noise/Protect); Garganacl (Impish, Leftovers, Purifying Salt: Salt Cure/Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Recover). Tsareena blocks priority while active. Tauros Close Combat into Archaludon deals 60.9-106.7% pre-Stamina and Tauros outspeeds it. Venusaur outspeeds Pelipper; Energy Ball at Pelipper’s shown 57% is only a possible KO. Preserve Venusaur for Swampert pressure when possible.

decisions.rationale: Garganacl faces double super-effective targeting from Tauros's Close Combat and Venusaur's Energy Ball. Switching Pelipper into slot 1 safety-absorbs Energy Ball (neutral) and CC (resisted) while setting Drizzle. Switching Archaludon (16% HP, slp) to Mega Swampert into slot 2 brings Swampert in unharmed. In Rain, Swift Swim Swampert (208 Speed) outspeeds both Tauros (max 167) and non-Sun Venusaur (max 132), setting up a clean end game.

Switching in Garganacl (slot 1 choice 1) brings a healthy 100% HP Pokémon onto the field. Its Purifying Salt ability grants complete immunity to Venusaur's Sleep Powder, unlike the 16% sleeping Archaludon. With Swampert active and fast in Rain, Garganacl gives us full health presence and status immunity to seal Game 1.
decisions.notebook:
Game 1: Opponent brought Charizard-Mega-Y (Timid, fainted), Venusaur (Modest, Focus Sash, Energy Ball/Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder/Protect), Raichu (Timid, fainted), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Jolly, Wacan Berry, Intimidate, CC/Liquidation/Aqua Jet/Protect). Unbrought: Kingambit, Sableye.
Garganacl's Purifying Salt makes it immune to Sleep Powder. Tauros drops its Def and SpD by 2 stages when using Close Combat.

decisions.rationale: Close Combat is a guaranteed KO on the revealed low-HP Archaludon despite its Stamina boost, before it can act. Energy Ball is Venusaur’s strongest legal pressure into Garganacl, dealing 58–106.3% and potentially removing it outright while preserving Venusaur’s crucial Grass coverage for Mega Swampert.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent roster/set information: Mega Swampert (Adamant, Swampertite); Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash, Drizzle: Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect); Archaludon (Modest, Wise Glasses, Stamina: Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect); Tsareena (Adamant, Miracle Seed, Queenly Majesty: Power Whip/High Jump Kick/Knock Off/Helping Hand); Galarian Slowking (Calm, Sitrus Berry, Regenerator: Sludge Bomb/Chilly Reception/Psychic Noise/Protect); Garganacl (Impish, Leftovers, Purifying Salt: Salt Cure/Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Recover). Tsareena blocks priority while active. Tauros Close Combat into Archaludon deals 42.6–72.7% through a +1 Defense Stamina boost and is guaranteed to KO from 15%. Venusaur Energy Ball into Garganacl deals 58–106.3%. Preserve Venusaur for Mega Swampert pressure when possible.

decisions.rationale: Swampert outspeeds both foes in rain (208 Speed) but takes 4x from Venusaur's Energy Ball. Using Protect safely blocks expected attacks directed at Swampert. Garganacl uses Salt Cure on Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (-2 Def/SpD), applying heavy immediate chip and 25% max HP residual damage per turn due to its Water typing. This sets up Swampert to cleanly finish Tauros next turn with High Horsepower.
decisions.notebook:
Game 1: Opponent brought Charizard-Mega-Y (fainted), Venusaur (Modest, Focus Sash, Energy Ball/Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder/Protect), Raichu (fainted), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Jolly, Wacan Berry, Intimidate, CC/Liquidation/Aqua Jet/Protect). Unbrought: Kingambit, Sableye.
- Garganacl's Purifying Salt grants status immunity (Sleep Powder fails against it).
- Tauros-Paldea-Aqua takes 25% max HP per turn from Salt Cure due to Water typing.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Tauros’s remaining bulk while Venusaur’s Energy Ball is a guaranteed KO on Mega Swampert from 50%, even through its full legal special-bulk range. This removes the rain-boosted Swift Swim threat immediately and leaves both attackers available to pressure Garganacl before Recover can stabilize it.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 1 sets: Mega Swampert (Adamant, Swampertite; Waterfall/High Horsepower/Ice Punch/Protect), Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash, Drizzle; Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect), Archaludon (Modest, Wise Glasses, Stamina; Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect), Garganacl (Impish, Leftovers, Purifying Salt; Salt Cure/Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Recover). Backline: Tsareena (Adamant, Miracle Seed, Queenly Majesty; Power Whip/High Jump Kick/Knock Off/Helping Hand), Galarian Slowking (Calm, Sitrus, Regenerator; Sludge Bomb/Chilly Reception/Psychic Noise/Protect). Tsareena blocks priority while active. Venusaur Energy Ball is guaranteed to KO Mega Swampert from 50%. Venusaur Energy Ball into Garganacl: 58–106.3%. Tauros Close Combat into Archaludon through +1 Stamina: 42.6–72.7%, guaranteed from 15%. Preserve Venusaur as the primary Swampert answer; account for Garganacl Recover and Wide Guard.

decisions.rationale: Swampert outspeeds under rain (208) and hits Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (-2 Def) with High Horsepower for 84-150% damage. Garganacl follows with Salt Cure on Tauros to guarantee the KO regardless of roll; if High Horsepower KOs outright, Salt Cure retargets Venusaur. Removing Tauros leaves Venusaur alone against Garganacl, who is immune to Sleep Powder via Purifying Salt and can stall out Energy Ball with Recover and Leftovers.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Venusaur’s Energy Ball removes Mega Swampert, the rain-speed threat. Close Combat chunks Garganacl heavily; after Swampert is gone, Venusaur moves before Garganacl and can finish it with Energy Ball next turn. Ice Punch does not KO full Venusaur.

Garganacl is at 100% HP with Purifying Salt (immune to Sleep Powder). Energy Ball from Modest Venusaur deals 49.3-87.9% to Garganacl, so Recover keeps Garganacl near full HP to comfortably win the 1v1 across future turns. If Archaludon wakes up, Draco Meteor (50.3-111%) plus end-of-turn Salt Cure chip (12.5%) has a high chance to KO Venusaur (76% HP) directly on Turn 10 to close out Game 1.
decisions.notebook:
Game 1: Opponent brought Charizard-Mega-Y (fainted), Venusaur (Modest, Focus Sash broken, Energy Ball/Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder/Protect), Raichu (fainted), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Jolly, Wacan Berry, Intimidate, CC/Liquidation/Aqua Jet/Protect). Unbrought: Kingambit, Sableye.
- Garganacl's Purifying Salt grants status immunity (Sleep Powder fails against it).
- Venusaur Chlorophyll inactive in Rain; base 80 Speed.

decisions.rationale: Energy Ball is the only productive action: it acts before Garganacl, is super-effective, and has an OHKO chance. Sleep Powder cannot status Purifying Salt Garganacl, while attacking Archaludon is ineffective and leaves Garganacl unchecked.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 1 sets: Mega Swampert (Adamant, Swampertite; Waterfall/High Horsepower/Ice Punch/Protect), Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash, Drizzle; Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect), Archaludon (Modest, Wise Glasses, Stamina; Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect), Garganacl (Impish, Leftovers, Purifying Salt; Salt Cure/Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Recover). Backline: Tsareena (Adamant, Miracle Seed, Queenly Majesty; Power Whip/High Jump Kick/Knock Off/Helping Hand), Galarian Slowking (Calm, Sitrus, Regenerator; Sludge Bomb/Chilly Reception/Psychic Noise/Protect). Tsareena blocks priority while active. Venusaur Energy Ball guarantees Mega Swampert KO from 50%. Venusaur Energy Ball into Garganacl is 58–106.3%; Venusaur always moves before Garganacl. Purifying Salt prevents nonvolatile status, so Sleep Powder cannot sleep Garganacl. Tauros Close Combat into +1 Stamina Archaludon is 42.6–72.7%, guaranteed from 15%. Preserve Venusaur as the primary Swampert answer; account for Garganacl Recover and Wide Guard.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is at 70% HP with Salt Cure active (12.5% end-of-turn damage). Archaludon's Draco Meteor deals 55.1-99.4% damage to Venusaur, and Garganacl's Salt Cure deals an additional 11.2-21.3%. Combined with end-of-turn Salt Cure chip (78.8% minimum total damage), this guarantees a KO on Venusaur if Draco Meteor hits. Purifying Salt protects Garganacl from Sleep Powder, ensuring game win.

Energy Ball Garganacl: it has the immediate KO chance at its displayed health, whereas Archaludon is not reliably removed by Energy Ball. If Garganacl falls, Venusaur can finish the already-weakened Archaludon while retaining a realistic survival line.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 1 sets: Mega Swampert (Adamant, Swampertite; Waterfall/High Horsepower/Ice Punch/Protect), Pelipper (Modest, Focus Sash, Drizzle; Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect), Archaludon (Modest, Wise Glasses, Stamina; Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect), Garganacl (Impish, Leftovers, Purifying Salt; Salt Cure/Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Recover). Backline: Tsareena (Adamant, Miracle Seed, Queenly Majesty; Power Whip/High Jump Kick/Knock Off/Helping Hand), Galarian Slowking (Calm, Sitrus, Regenerator; Sludge Bomb/Chilly Reception/Psychic Noise/Protect). Tsareena blocks priority while active. Venusaur Energy Ball guarantees Mega Swampert KO from 50%. Venusaur Energy Ball into Garganacl is 58–106.3%; Venusaur always moves before Garganacl. Purifying Salt prevents nonvolatile status, so Sleep Powder cannot sleep Garganacl. Tauros Close Combat into +1 Stamina Archaludon is 42.6–72.7%, guaranteed from 15%. Preserve Venusaur as the primary Swampert answer; account for Garganacl Recover and Wide Guard. Archaludon has used Draco Meteor twice, leaving it heavily Special Attack-reduced; Venusaur Energy Ball into it is only 9.1–17.6%.

reflections.summary: Swampert-Mega was brought into a team featuring a Focus Sash Venusaur with Energy Ball, resulting in Swampert's early KO and forcing a narrow endgame where Archaludon barely clutched the win.
reflections.adjustment: Break Venusaur's Focus Sash with Garganacl or Archaludon and neutralize its Grass coverage before safe deployment of Swampert-Mega, or pivot through Garganacl's Sleep Powder immunity to control the board safely.
reflections.notebook:
Revealed Sets:
- Charizard-Y: Timid, Charizardite Y (Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Air Slash, Protect).
- Venusaur: Modest, Focus Sash, Chlorophyll (Energy Ball, Sludge Bomb, Sleep Powder, Protect).
- Tauros-Paldea-Aqua: Jolly, Wacan Berry, Intimidate (Close Combat, Liquidation, Aqua Jet, Protect).
- Raichu: Timid, Sitrus Berry, LightningRod (Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, Protect).
- Unbrought G1: Kingambit, Sableye.

Strategic Facts & Tendencies:
- Opponent leads Sun core (Charizard-Y + Venusaur) or Raichu disruption against Rain.
- Garganacl's Purifying Salt grants immunity to Sleep Powder.
- In Rain, Venusaur loses Chlorophyll Speed, enabling Archaludon and Swampert-Mega to outspeed it once Focus Sash is broken.

reflections.summary: Lost the endgame because Archaludon was left alive at 15% and Venusaur could not finish it; once Tauros fell, Draco Meteor removed Venusaur. The Charizard-Y rain matchup was also poorly aligned, as Pelipper could restore rain after sun.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Tauros available to Close Combat chipped Archaludon, even if that means using Venusaur to pressure Mega Swampert first. Reconsider Mega Charizard Y versus this rain core; its weather advantage is temporary and it is a fragile bring into Pelipper/Swampert/Garganacl.
reflections.notebook: Opponent brought the Pelipper/Mega Swampert/Archaludon/Garganacl rain shell in Game 1. Pelipper is Focus Sash and has Tailwind; Archaludon is Wise Glasses Stamina with Draco Meteor; Garganacl has Leftovers, Recover, Wide Guard, and Purifying Salt, so it cannot be slept. Preserve Tauros as an Archaludon finisher and Venusaur as the main Mega Swampert check. Plan for Pelipper to re-establish rain after Charizard Y enters; consider a non-Charizard-Y game plan if available.
